findings.title: Redefining `self.downsize` overwrites the 4-argument version (Ruby has no method overloading)
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` is defined twice: first on line 145 with signature `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` and then again on line 149 with signature `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. Ruby does not support method overloading by arity, so the second definition completely replaces the first. Existing callers that pass `(from, to, max_width, max_height)` (or `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)`) will now either fail with `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (5 for 3..4)` or treat `max_height` as `opts` (causing `TypeError: no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer` when `opts[:allow_animation]` is accessed) and pass only `max_width` as `dimensions`.

findings.title: `gifsicle --resize-fit` does not accept percentage dimensions like `"80%"`
findings.body: `UploadsController#create_upload` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)`. When `allow_animation` is true and the file has a `.gif` extension, `OptimizedImage.optimize` dispatches to `downsize_instructions_animated`, which delegates to `resize_instructions_animated` and invokes `gifsicle ... --resize-fit #{dimensions}`. `gifsicle`'s `--resize-fit` only accepts `WxH` pixel dimensions (e.g. `100x100`, `_x100`, `100x_`), not a percentage like `80%` (for scaling, `gifsicle` uses `--scale 0.8`). As a result, `gifsicle` exits with a non-zero status on every iteration and animated GIFs larger than `max_image_size_kb` are never downsized.

findings.title: Client-side size check ignores `max_attachment_size_kb` and `max_image_size_kb` site settings
findings.body: `validateUploadedFile` previously checked `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, which enforced `max_attachment_size_kb` for non-image attachments and `max_image_size_kb` for images. Replacing it with a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10 MB) means non-image attachments up to 10 MB now pass client-side validation even when `max_attachment_size_kb` is smaller (and the server does not downsize non-images, so the upload is uploaded in full only to be rejected server-side), and admins who configure `max_attachment_size_kb` or `max_image_size_kb` above 10 MB will have uploads blocked on the client with a misleading 10 MB limit error.
